title: Backing Into People
hook: Mid-reverse. A coat just stepped into the aisle.
scene: Heavy rain under flat gray overcast. You are at the wheel of the Menace, nose-in in a marked stall, ordinary cars parked tight on both sides so the aisle stays hidden until your rear clears the bay. Reverse lamps are already lit. The Beetle is partway out, wheels cut. One dark coat has stepped into that aisle from the side you have to check. They are not looking at your lamps. Yield is the whole reverse, not a glance before you roll.
decision: You are mid-reverse out of the stall and someone has entered the aisle. How do you leave?

options.text: Reverse now — they will see the lamps and move
options.result: You come out on a guess. They do not see the lamps in the rain. The plow is the wrong end for this. You write a coat into a stall exit. The lot did not need that sound.

options.text: Honk the whole reverse so they know a car is coming
options.result: You back up shouting. They jump and scatter into the other aisle lane. A primer car has to lift. Sound got them off your paint and onto someone else's.

options.text: Wait until they pass, then creep out and stop if anyone new enters the aisle
options.result: You wait once and then commit. A third coat steps off the curb after you are already rolling. Waiting is not the same as checking the whole time you move.

options.text: Wait them out, check both ways, creep, and be ready to plant it the whole reverse
options.result: You let the coat clear. You look both ways. You creep. A second person appears and you plant it. They pass. You finish into an empty aisle. The stall stays a stall.

debrief: Angled and straight-in stalls back into a live aisle. People in that aisle own it until they are gone. Wait for them to clear, then creep.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part two
source.teaching_target: When backing out of angled or perpendicular parking, yield to people and traffic; creep and be ready to stop.

image_brief.camera_pose: Low three-quarter from behind the Menace, human eye height in the drive aisle. NOT high overhead, NOT architecture, NOT bird's-eye. Rear bumper and white reverse lamps nearest the lens; stall and plow recede. Beetle straddles the stall mouth: rear third in the aisle, nose still in the bay. Pedestrian in the open aisle on the reverse path, not against a wall.

image_brief.foreground: one dark-coated pedestrian in the open aisle on the reverse path, mid-stride, several feet from the bumper, not along a wall
image_brief.midground: two parallel white stall lines to a curb wall; full gray sedans in the stalls immediately left and right; plow at the far stall end
image_brief.background: heavy rain, flat gray overcast daylight, visible gray sky, wet downtown lot, no night, no lot-lamp key light
